messages:
Aisha (Design): quick design check :eyes: — the threshold quick-edit panel in the Alerting SLO flow feels really dense on mobile/narrow widths. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/alerting-quick-edit
Aisha (Design): question: do we want a compact two-line row with an inline value editor, or keep the current single-line with a modal editor? Pros/cons: inline is faster but might break keyboard/aria; modal makes accidental edits less likely.
Matt (Eng-Frontend): inline editor is doable but we need to guard focus and scroll. long channel names will push controls off-screen. we could clamp names and show full on hover.
Matt (Eng-Frontend): implementation-wise we can virtualize the list and allow expanding a single row into edit mode. need to avoid layout shift when kv cache updates cause re-render.
Sam (Accessibility): from ARIA perspective inline edit must expose role="spinbutton" or role="textbox" with aria-label="threshold value" and announce changes via aria-live. also ensure color contrast for the delta badge (green/red) meets 4.5:1.
Julia (PM): product preference: inline for power users but only in "compact mode" behind a toggle. default stays single-line with a clear edit affordance (pencil) that opens modal.
Julia (PM): important: add a confirmation step for threshold reductions that affect paging (toggling to lower threshold).
Priya (DesignOps): copy nits: "Mute" vs "Snooze" — we should keep one term across the console. suggest "Snooze notifications" with tooltip: "Temporarily pause alerts for this channel".
Aisha (Design): also suggestion: move the preview button into the header of the SLO editor, not per-row. the preview pane should show sample incidents timeline rather than just last alert.
Matt (Eng-Frontend): ok re preview — server can return sample traces. small note: preview can be expensive; cache per-prompt and invalidate on threshold/value change.
Sam (Accessibility): keyboard flow: tab order should be row checkbox -> name -> threshold -> edit -> channel menu. when inline editing opens, focus must land on input and Escape cancels.
Aisha (Design): proposal summary:
- Default: single-line rows with pencil modal for edits
- Compact mode (optional): two-line rows with inline spinbutton for quick edits
- Preview moved to editor header; aria-live region for preview status
- Consolidate term to "Snooze notifications"
- Confirmation modal for threshold reductions that may trigger paging
Aisha (Design): can we get engineering feasibility and a rough effort estimate? :thumbsup: \nMatt (Eng-Frontend): feasibility: medium. modal path is low effort. inline compact mode ~2 sprints (list virtualization + focus handling + tests). preview header + caching ~1 sprint infra + 1 frontend sprint.
Matt (Eng-Frontend): small implementation note:
```
// keyboard handler pseudo
onKeyDown(e) {
  if (e.key === 'Escape') cancelEdit();
  if (e.key === 'Enter') commitEdit();
}
// aria for spinbutton
<input role="spinbutton" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-label="threshold percentage" />
```
Priya (DesignOps): I'll update Figma and copy. Aisha, can you draft microcopy for the confirmation modal? I'll push to the doc.
Aisha (Design): draft modal copy: "Lowering this threshold may increase alerts sent to channels. Are you sure you want to continue?" buttons: "Cancel" / "Lower threshold" (danger).
Julia (PM): also capture telemetry: event names: alert_threshold_edit.start, .commit, .cancel, and preview.open/close.
Matt (Eng-Frontend): noted. I'll add feature flag 'compact_threshold_edit' and track rollout.
ui-bot: Deployed design update to the staging figma file and created a follow-up task: https://github.com/redwoodinference/ui/issues/452
Aisha (Design): thanks all — let's sync on Monday 10am to review updated figma and a11y checklist. :calendar:
